Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Hon’ble Ramesh Chandra Khulbe, J.

assisted by Ms. Chetna Latwal, Advocate 
present for the applicant. 
 Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate 
General assisted by Ms. Mamta Joshi, Brief 
Holder present for the State. 
 The applicant has been convicted and 
sentenced to life imprisonment under Section 
302 IPC. 
 Heard Ms. Pushpa Joshi, learned Senior 
Counsel for the applicant and Mr. V.K. Jemini, 
Deputy Advocate General on the bail 
application.

after perusal of the lower court record and 
judgment passed by the learned Trial Court, we 
are not inclined to release the applicant on 
bail. 
 Bail application is hereby rejected.

cause list.

Mr. J. S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate 
General with Mr. Rakesh Kumar Joshi, 
learned Brief Holder for the State of 
Uttarakhand.
This is an application for short term bail 
filed by the applicant – Bala Devi on the 
ground that her daughter is suffering from 
various ailments including hepatitis.
It is also submitted by Mrs. Pushpa 
Joshi, the learned Senior Advocate appearing 
for the appellants that the appellant – Bala 
Devi was granted parole and in the 
meantime, she has already surrendered before 
the Jail Authorities concerned. There is no 
allegation against her that she misused the 
liberty granted by us to her.
We have perused the medical certificates 
and of the view that the applicant should be  granted short term bail for a period of 30
days, hence this Court is inclined to allow the 
application for short term bail. 
Let the applicant –Bala Devi be released 
on short term bail for a period of 30 days,
which shall be reckoned from the date of her
release from jail on such suitable terms and 
conditions, as deems fit and proper by the 
learned 5th Additional Session Judge, District 
– Dehradun.
On expiry of 30 days, applicant – Bala 
Devi shall surrender before the trial Court,
who in turn, shall send him to jail. In case, he 
fails to surrender after expiry of 30 days, the 
learned 5th Additional Session Judge, District 
– Dehradun shall issue Non Bailable Warrant 
against the applicant – Bala Devi. 
In that view of the matter, the 
application for short term bail is allowed for 
a period of 30 days. 
List this matter on 14.02.2023 along 
with connected matter.
In the meantime, learned counsel for the 
State shall file objection to the application 
filed, under Section 389 of the Code of 
Criminal Procedure, by Chotu alias 
Shikander.
The Short Term Bail Application (IA 
No. 341 of 2022) stands disposed of.
 
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.) 
07.12.2022

orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
IA No.346 of 2026 For Third Bail Application
In
Criminal Appeal No. 42 of 2018
Bala Devi and another ...... Appellants
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ..... Respondent
Present:
Ms. Neelima Mishra Joshi, Advocate for the appellants.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, A.G.A. for the State. 
Coram: Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Hon’ble Siddhartha Sah, J.
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The instant appeal has been preferred against 
judgment and order dated 25.01.2018, passed in Sessions Trial 
No.151 of 2007, State Vs. Bala Devi and others, by the court of 
Fifth Additional Sessions Judge, District Dehradun. By it, the 
appellants have been convicted and sentenced under Sections 302 
and 201 IPC. 
2. Heard.
3. This appeal has already been admitted.
4. List in due course for final hearing. 
5. Heard on Third Bail Application (IA) No.346 of 
2018
6. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that 
co-convict, having similar role, has already been granted bail; the 
appellants have already undergone more than half of the sentence
imposed upon them; there are less chances of the appeal being 
heard in near future.
7. These facts are admitted by learned State Counsel. 2
8. Having considered the period of incarceration and 
other attending factors, we are of the view that it is a case in 
which the execution of sentence should be suspended and the 
appellants be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.
10. The sentence appealed against is suspended 
during the pendency of the appeal.
11. The appellants- Bala Devi and Mohar Singh @ 
Mohan Singh be released on bail during the pendency of the 
appeal on their executing a personal bond and furnishing two 
reliable sureties, each of the like amount, by each one of them, to 
the satisfaction of the court concerned. 
(Siddhartha Sah, J.) (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 18.04.2026 
 Ravi Bisht
